questions.stem: As of 2024, how many UNESCO World Heritage Sites are located in India?
questions.explanation: India has 42 UNESCO World Heritage Sites as of 2024: 34 Cultural + 7 Natural + 1 Mixed (Khangchendzonga NP). Recent additions: Santiniketan (2023, cultural), Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas — Belur, Halebid, Somanathapura (2023, cultural), Moidams of Ahom (2024 — first natural/cultural site from NE). India ranks 6th globally in number of sites (Italy #1 with 59). Italy and China competing for #1; France, Germany, Spain round out top-5.

questions.stem: Which was India's FIRST UNESCO World Heritage Site, inscribed in 1983?

options.option_text: Ajanta Caves, Ellora Caves, Agra Fort and Taj Mahal — all inscribed in 1983

questions.explanation: India's FIRST batch of 4 UNESCO WHS inscriptions happened in 1983: (1) Ajanta Caves (Maharashtra — Buddhist caves, 2nd c. BCE-6th c. CE), (2) Ellora Caves (Maharashtra — Buddhist/Hindu/Jain), (3) Agra Fort (UP), (4) Taj Mahal (UP — Shah Jahan for Mumtaz Mahal, completed ~1653). In 1984, Sun Temple Konark and Mahabalipuram group were added. Khajuraho and Goa churches came in 1986. Red Fort was inscribed in 2007 — fairly late.

questions.stem: The Kailash Temple (Cave 16) at Ellora, the world's largest monolithic rock-cut structure, was commissioned by which king?
questions.explanation: The Kailash Temple (Cave 16, Ellora, Maharashtra) is a monolith carved top-down from a single basalt rock by the Rashtrakuta king KRISHNA I (r. 756-774 CE). Dedicated to Shiva, modelled after Mount Kailash. Covers 2x the area of the Parthenon in Athens and is 1.5x its height. An estimated 200,000 tonnes of rock were removed. One of the greatest engineering and artistic achievements in human history. Ellora overall has 34 caves: 12 Buddhist (600-700 CE, south), 17 Hindu (600-900 CE, middle), 5 Jain (800-1000 CE, north) — a unique coexistence.

questions.stem: The Brihadeshwara Temple at Thanjavur, a UNESCO WHS, was built by which Chola emperor?
questions.explanation: The Brihadeshwara (Peruvudaiyar, RajaRajeshwaram) Temple at Thanjavur (Tamil Nadu) was built by RAJA RAJA CHOLA I between 1003-1010 CE. It is one of the 'Great Living Chola Temples' (UNESCO WHS 1987, extended 2004). Features: the main vimana (tower) is ~216 ft high, one of the tallest of any Indian temple; crowned by a 80-tonne single-stone kalash on top; the massive Nandi bull statue at the entrance weighs 20 tonnes. Other Living Chola Temples: Gangaikondacholapuram (Rajendra I, 1035 CE), Airavatesvara at Darasuram (Rajaraja II, 12th c.).

questions.stem: The Sun Temple at Konark was built in the 13th century by which king of which dynasty?
questions.explanation: The Sun Temple at Konark (Odisha) was built by King NARASIMHADEVA I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty around 1250 CE — to commemorate his military victory over Muslim invaders. Designed in the form of a gigantic CHARIOT with 12 pairs of intricately carved wheels (representing 12 months/zodiac signs) and 7 running horses (representing days of the week or the Sun god's chariot). UNESCO WHS 1984. The main shikhara collapsed long ago; only the jagmohan (audience hall) and the dance hall remain. Called the 'Black Pagoda' by European sailors (as a navigation landmark).

questions.stem: The Khajuraho Group of Monuments, famous for their erotic sculptures and Nagara-style temples, were built by which dynasty?
questions.explanation: The Khajuraho temples (MP) were built by the Chandela Rajputs between 950-1050 CE — originally 85 temples; only 25 survive today (20 Hindu + 5 Jain). Most famous: Kandariya Mahadev (tallest, 31m, dedicated to Shiva), Lakshmana, Vishwanath, Devi Jagadambi, Chitragupta. UNESCO WHS 1986. The erotic sculptures (only ~10% of total sculptures) represent the temple's tantric associations, or celebrate life / Kama (one of the 4 purusharthas). The temples were 'rediscovered' by British officer T.S. Burt in 1838 after being hidden by jungle for centuries. Classical example of Nagara architecture.

questions.stem: Hampi, a UNESCO WHS, was the capital of which medieval empire?
questions.explanation: Hampi (Karnataka, on the Tungabhadra river) was the capital of the VIJAYANAGARA Empire (1336-1565/1646 CE). Founded by Harihara I and Bukka Raya I of the Sangama dynasty in 1336 under sage Vidyaranya's blessing. At its peak under Krishnadevaraya (1509-29), Hampi was one of the world's largest cities (500,000 people). Destroyed after the Battle of Talikota (1565) when the Deccan Sultanates combined to rout the Vijayanagara army. Key monuments: Virupaksha Temple (active since 7th c.), Vittala Temple (musical stone pillars, stone chariot), Lotus Mahal, Elephant Stables, Hazara Rama Temple. UNESCO WHS 1986.

questions.stem: Which is the ONLY mixed (natural + cultural) UNESCO World Heritage Site in India?
questions.explanation: Khangchendzonga National Park (Sikkim) — inscribed in 2016 — is India's ONLY MIXED UNESCO WHS (both natural AND cultural criteria). Natural: includes Mt Khangchendzonga (8,586m — world's 3rd-highest peak, and sacred to Sikkimese Buddhists), glaciers, lakes, diverse flora/fauna. Cultural: sacred landscapes of the indigenous Lepcha people and Sikkimese Buddhists — Khangchendzonga is revered as 'Mount Kinchinjonga' by locals and worshipped. Globally, only ~40 mixed WHS exist. Sundarbans, Western Ghats, Nanda Devi & VoF are all pure-natural.

questions.stem: The Jagannath Temple of Puri and the annual Rath Yatra are associated with which deity form?

options.option_text: Vishnu (Krishna as Jagannath, with Balabhadra and Subhadra)

questions.explanation: The Jagannath Temple at Puri (Odisha) is dedicated to Lord Jagannath ('Lord of the Universe' — a form of Vishnu/Krishna), along with his elder brother BALABHADRA and sister SUBHADRA. Built in the 12th c. by Anantavarman Chodaganga Deva of the Eastern Ganga dynasty. One of the CHAR DHAM of Hinduism (Puri + Rameswaram + Dwarka + Badrinath). The RATH YATRA (annual chariot festival, June-July) is world-famous — three huge wooden chariots (Nandighosha, Taladhwaja, Darpadalana) pull the deities the 3 km journey to Gundicha Temple and back. The English word 'juggernaut' derives from Jagannath. NOT a UNESCO WHS yet but on tentative list.

questions.stem: Dholavira, one of the five largest Harappan sites and a 2021 UNESCO WHS, is located in which state?
questions.explanation: Dholavira is located on Khadir Bet island in the Great Rann of Kutch, Gujarat. Discovered 1968, excavated 1989-2005 by RS Bisht (ASI). Features: a tripartite layout (Citadel, Middle Town, Lower Town), an ingenious water harvesting system with 16 reservoirs, and a famous 10-character 'Dholavira Signboard' — possibly the oldest signboard in the world. Inscribed as India's 40th UNESCO WHS on 27 July 2021. OTHER KEY HARAPPAN SITES: Mohenjo-daro (now Pakistan), Harappa (Pakistan), Lothal (Gujarat — world's earliest dockyard), Rakhigarhi (Haryana — largest), Kalibangan (Rajasthan — ploughed field, fire altars), Banawali (Haryana), Surkotada (Gujarat — horse remains).
